title: A part-source 2D cut that enters a neighbouring part has no op finding and posts on a turned stock

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens:** the laws a 2D operation carries on a part source (`Mark` for Engrave / Trace, `Keep` for the whole-model pocket family, `Section` for picks) read only the **source entity's** mesh. When the setup holds a second part and the cut on part B reaches into part A, the operation has no finding for A. With the stock aligned the program sim blocks the post; with the stock **turned** (the sim refuses to judge) nothing judges A.

Found by M5's review of PR #1615 (pullrequestreview-5900976523, note 2): two parts side by side, a Trace on B whose flank runs 2.3 mm into the taller part A:

| stock | result |
|---|---|
| aligned | the program sim refuses (worst 2.00 mm) |
| turned 90 deg about Z | the op records **no Gouge for A** (in that probe the post was blocked only by an unrelated rapid) |

It predates #1615 and applies equally to `Section`-law kinds on B.

**Expected:** a part-source 2D operation is judged against every part the setup holds, not only the one its source names: its own law against its source (unchanged), and the plain solid law against the setup's other parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`, the mesh the program sim judges against; fixtures and a stock-only model left out). A cut into a neighbour is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on the move on both stocks.

**Where:** `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` (`keep_parts`, today filled only for a stock source by `keep_law::parts_in_stock`) and the two frame arms of `run_job` in `generate.rs`. #1607 widens `keep_parts` to every 2D kind on a **stock** source on top of PR #1615's branch; this is the same mechanism for a **part** source, so it should stack on #1607 (or land after it) rather than touch those lines in parallel. For Engrave / Trace the neighbour gets no mark budget (the mark is on the source part); note that the sim's mark credit currently holds a neighbour to the budget, so the operation would be the stricter judge there.

**Done means:** the two-part probe above is refused on the operation by name on both stocks, for Engrave, Trace and one `Section` kind; a legal cut on B that stays clear of A still posts on both; pinned through generate and the post, mutation-checked; decision recorded.

Related: #1595, #1603, #1607, PR #1615 (`docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`, "Notes for the maintainer").
